tagline: Lake remnants and ancient duck decoys beyond a railway town
intro: The Lovelock Cave Back Country Byway runs for 20 miles past remains of Lake Lahontan. The Bureau of Land Management classifies it as a Type I and Type II Back Country Byway and recommends two to three hours for the trip. Its destination has yielded 2,000-year-old duck decoys, baskets and textiles, the archaeological finds behind BLM’s description of the cave as the cradle of Great Basin archaeology.

At the town end of the journey, transport changed Lovelock twice. The Central Pacific Railroad’s arrival in 1868 brought the town’s foundation; in 1983, Interstate 80 bypassed old U.S. Route 40 through downtown and drew business away from the center. The city subsequently promoted its historic buildings as heritage attractions.
Begin in Lovelock with the wooden depot, relocated across Broadway Avenue, then the Marzen ranch house near town. Beyond town lies Lovelock Cave, where a self-guided nature trail explores the area.

moments.title: Lovelock depot
moments.text: Lovelock’s depot combines a baggage room in its lower southern section with a taller northern section containing the waiting room, agent’s office and living quarters. Built in 1880, it became a regular stop for transcontinental trains. Amtrak’s California Zephyr stopped here until May 11, 1997, before Union Pacific proposed demolition in 1998. Union Pacific instead donated the building and the projected demolition cost to the city. Lovelock moved it across Broadway Avenue in 1999 and completed restoration in 2000. Finials, braces, brackets and flat board trim give both wooden sections their elaborate detail.

moments.title: Marzen House
moments.text: Ornate cutout window moldings and corner boards decorate the two-story Marzen House, a ranch residence with a low hipped roof. The Italianate house’s balanced exterior is clad in shiplap, initially painted white, with double-hung wooden windows beneath arch moldings. Joseph Marzen built it in 1875. He used Humboldt River water to irrigate land for wheat at Big Meadows. After its National Register listing, the empty house was moved to the edge of the ranch for use as a museum. The entrance has Victorian double doors beneath a frosted-glass transom, part of the house’s decorative design.

moments.title: Lovelock Cave
moments.text: Duck decoys, baskets and textiles are among the 2,000-year-old objects recovered from Lovelock Cave. Many of the artifacts are displayed in museums across the United States. BLM calls the cave the cradle of Great Basin archaeology. At the cave itself, interpretive signs and a self-guided nature trail provide ways to explore the site.

practical: Lovelock Cave: Portions of the 20-mile byway may require a high-clearance vehicle. (checked 2026-10-11)
